name: coldCatWormholePizza
source:
It was a bit cold this morning. My damn cat pushed my door open and let all the heat escape. My toasty little oven room was now a refrigerator box. I yawned and stretched out before getting up. 
 
 The morning felt typical. Go to the kitchen. Feed the cat. Start my coffee maker. Then I went back to my room and opened the blinds. A focal point of distorted landscape rested right outside the window. 
 
 It had finally happened. I had gone crazy. Now, I just needed to adopt a few more cats. 
 
 I flicked the blinds open and close a few more times. Nope, still there. So I threw on my winter coat and walked into my backyard. Wherever I looked into it, the behind it was distorted. My human instinct took over and I found the nearest stick to poke it with. I moved the stick into the center and the tip began to disappear. Weird! 
 
 I dropped the stick and found a rock instead. Angling myself to not hit my house, I threw the rock into the hole. It disappeared! Chills started to run through my body. I had found a gateway to somewhere. This would be famous. It would make me famous! 
 
 While daydreaming about the people I'd get to meet and history I would make, I failed to see the solid object flying towards my face. The rock I had throw returned and hit me right on the nose. I cried in pain and yelled at the thing. 
 
 `` Hey! That hurt! You got some nerve throwing rocks through a hole!'' 
 
 I realized the irony immediately and a minute later a note slipped through. 
 
 `` My apologies for throwing a rock through a wormhole. I should have remembered Rule # 1. Do n't throw objects through a wormhole where you do n't know what's on the other end. Let that be a lesson to you.'' The note had an arrow pointing towards the edge of the page. I flipped it over. 
 
 `` Send money; receive pizza.'' 
 
 I ran back inside and grab a 5, then returned and threw it in. A box popped out a few minutes later and I opened it to find the most amazing looking deluxe style pizza of my life. It was beyond delicious! I had never tasted anything so great! And that gave me an idea... 
 
 Wormhole Pizza. The business that would end my monotonous nothing of a career and catapult me into a world of excitement. I ran back inside and began planning.

Perspective: The Narrator's Cat (Unnamed)

In the early hours of a crisp morning, I, the cat, stretched languidly on the warm carpet in my human's room. Basking in the toasty warmth, I could sense the rhythmic rise and fall of my human's chest as they slept peacefully. Unbeknownst to me, this was a fleeting moment of comfort before I would disturb their slumber and plunge them into a peculiar adventure.

As dawn broke, I cautiously padded towards the door that led to the hallway, my whiskers twitching at the scent of fresh coffee wafting from the kitchen. With a casual swipe of my tail, I dislodged the door just enough for a cool draft to creep into the room, transforming it into a refrigerator box. My human stirred restlessly in their sleep, but the fragrant aroma of coffee soon overpowered the chill, and they rose to greet the day.

With my morning ritual complete, I returned to my perch by the window, watching idly as the blinds swayed gently in the breeze. My human's gaze flickered towards the distorted landscape outside, but I paid it no heed, focusing instead on a bird that dared to invade my territory. The scene outside suddenly captured their attention once more, and with a frown, they ventured into the backyard.

As they approached the strange hole in the ground, I felt a mixture of curiosity and concern. My human had always been drawn to oddities, but this one seemed particularly dangerous. With a resigned sigh, I settled down on the window ledge, content to observe from afar as my human threw objects into the seemingly bottomless pit.

The moment the rock struck me in the face, however, I sprang into action. I darted towards the backyard, my claws clicking loudly on the cold concrete. My human stood frozen at the sight of their injured companion, and I could sense their confusion and worry. Then, from the depths of the hole, a note emerged, apologizing for the inadvertent attack and offering pizza in exchange for money.

I watched as my human sent away some of their hard-earned coins, and minutes later, a delicious pizza was delivered through the mysterious portal. The tantalizing smell wafted towards me, and I could see the spark of inspiration in my human's eyes. And so, "Wormhole Pizza" was born, a testament to the strange and wonderful world that exists just beyond the reach of my paw.

From my vantage point by the window, I continue to observe the comings and goings of this peculiar place, ever curious about the adventures that await on the other side of the wormhole.
